title: Quantinuum and Oracle Partner to Bring Helios Quantum Computer to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantinuum and Oracle signed a multi-year deal to install the 98-qubit Helios trapped-ion processor physically inside a U.S. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data center as a managed OCI quantum service — Quantinuum's first on-premises placement inside a hyperscaler's AI data center, co-located with NVIDIA GPU clusters and drawing only ~60 kW.

insights.claim: Quantinuum's 98-qubit Helios processor will be installed physically inside a U.S.-based Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data center and sold as a managed OCI quantum service under a multi-year strategic partnership.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Selling quantum as a managed hyperscaler service collapses the enterprise procurement cycle from a capital project to a cloud SKU.

insights.claim: This is Quantinuum's first on-premises deployment inside a major hyperscale public cloud provider's AI data center ecosystem, setting a template rivals will be pressured to match with AWS, Azure or Google.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Expect competing quantum vendors to announce hyperscaler co-location deals next; first-mover placement inside AI data centers is becoming the sector's key land-grab.
insights.quote: the deal represents Quantinuum’s first on-premises deployment inside a major hyperscale public cloud provider’s AI data center ecosystem.
insights.locator: Led by Quantinuum President and CEO

insights.claim: Co-locating Helios inside OCI wires the QPU directly into Oracle's compute, storage, networking, identity and security governance frameworks, removing the need for specialized hardware installation or local facility management by the customer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Identity and governance integration is what makes quantum consumable by regulated enterprises — the unglamorous unlock that matters more than qubit count.
insights.quote: allowing developers to orchestrate hybrid workflows without specialized hardware installation or local facility management.

insights.claim: Oracle plans to preview the managed OCI quantum service in the coming months, pairing Quantinuum's development environment with open-source hybrid programming frameworks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The preview date is the near-term catalyst; watch pricing disclosure, which would be the first public benchmark for hyperscaler quantum service economics.
insights.quote: Oracle plans to preview the managed OCI quantum service in upcoming months

insights.claim: Helios is a third-generation trapped-ion system using a Quantum Charge-Coupled Device architecture with barium (137Ba+) hyperfine qubits, delivering all-to-all connectivity, 99.921% average two-qubit gate fidelity and demonstrations of up to 48 logical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: All-to-all connectivity plus 99.921% two-qubit fidelity is the trapped-ion differentiator against superconducting rivals that must burn circuit depth on SWAP gates.
insights.quote: utilizes a Quantum Charge-Coupled Device (QCCD) architecture with barium (137Ba+) hyperfine qubits, delivering all-to-all connectivity, 99.921% average two-qubit gate fidelity, and demonstrations running up to 48 logical qubits.

insights.claim: Helios encodes 48 logical qubits out of 98 physical qubits, an unusually low physical-to-logical overhead ratio of roughly 2:1 for an error-corrected machine.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Physical-to-logical overhead is the real scaling cost driver; a ~2:1 ratio, if sustained, materially changes the qubit counts needed for useful applications.

insights.claim: Helios draws approximately 60 kW excluding external HVAC, less than one percent of the power consumed by leading top-tier supercomputers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: In a data-center market constrained by megawatts rather than capex, a 60 kW accelerator is a rounding error on the power budget — the strongest commercial argument for putting a QPU next to GPUs.
insights.quote: Helios uses less than one percent of the power consumed by leading top-tier supercomputers

insights.claim: Positioning the QPU as a low-power complementary resource alongside NVIDIA GPU clusters reframes quantum as an accelerator inside AI infrastructure rather than a replacement for classical computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The accelerator framing is how quantum gets budget: it competes for a slice of AI infrastructure spend rather than needing its own new line item.
insights.locator: offering a low-power complementary QPU resource

insights.claim: The Oracle-Quantinuum collaboration targets enterprise, research laboratory and academic workloads in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling and large-scale optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: These four verticals define where the first paying quantum cloud customers will come from; map exposure through the pharma and financial-services buyers rather than the hardware vendors.
insights.locator: The collaboration focuses on enabling enterprise

insights.claim: The deal is sponsored at senior level by Quantinuum President and CEO Dr. Rajeeb Hazra and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure EVP Mahesh Thiagarajan.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: EVP-level sponsorship at OCI suggests this is a cloud product roadmap commitment rather than a research-lab curiosity.
insights.locator: Led by Quantinuum President and CEO
